analysis:
The changed file is a test-only Swift file (provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Prompting/GLM5NextPromptPolicyTests.swift). It adds no production code, endpoints, key handling, attestation or authorization paths, so no threat-model asset or boundary behavior changes directly.

The head side adds test coverage for the `thinking` control spelling (`{type: enabled|disabled}`, bool), null-tolerant handling of `include_reasoning`/`thinking`, and a null/summary-tolerant `reasoning` object. It adds contradiction cases (`thinking` disabled + reasoning effort high; `thinking` enabled + `reasoning_effort` none). It adds fail-closed malformed cases at head lines 484-502, including `thinking` as a string, an int, `adaptive`, `budget_tokens`, or a null type, plus `reasoning: true`, `summary: verbose`, `generate_summary`, and `context: all_turns`. Exclusion cases still map to the 400 client error that never leaves the provider (head lines 352-367). Together these tests strengthen a fail-closed prompt-control parser, which supports TB-007 and T-056 expectations that the provider does not misrepresent hidden reasoning. They do not touch the T-041 cache scope.

The only remaining concern is for the integration pass: the corresponding production change in GLM5NextPromptPolicy.RawControls is not in the supplied evidence. I could not verify that it matches these tests, for example that a `thinking: {type: enabled}` body is never misparsed into a state that differs between the coordinator path and the local HTTP path. The tests do exercise both paths through remoteAndLocalInputs. The patch excerpt notes added lines at head 645-897, but the supplied head text stops at line 508, so that tail region was not reviewed. It is probably test fixtures and helpers. No security regression is identified in the supplied lines.
